question_v1.title: ELN 2022 AML recommendations — evidence brief
question_v1.question: Which diagnostic, genetic-risk and response-assessment information should be reviewed before an AML case is discussed under a departmental pathway?
question_v1.scope: AML departmental evidence review and individual applicability.
question_v1.intended_use: Inform a reviewed case-readiness pathway; no automatic treatment recommendation.

appraisal_v1.population: Adults with AML; this is an expert recommendations document, not a randomized patient cohort.
appraisal_v1.intervention: Not applicable: recommendations and classification framework.
appraisal_v1.comparator: Not applicable: no experimental treatment comparison.
appraisal_v1.outcome: Updated disease and genetic-risk classification Genomic diagnostics and measurable residual disease assessment Revised response criteria and management recommendations
appraisal_v1.timepoint: As reported in the dated publication; check the source version.
appraisal_v1.findings: The 2022 panel update addresses advances in molecular classification, genomic diagnostics, measurable residual disease and AML therapies. Its abstract identifies revisions to genetic-risk classification and response criteria; it is a reference for documenting the framework used in a case assessment, not an automatic classifier.
appraisal_v1.uncertainty: Bounded abstract/source-record appraisal. Full methods and current evidence have not been comprehensively reviewed.
appraisal_v1.limitations: The PubMed citation and abstract were verified. The publisher full-text page returned a security-verification 403, so detailed tables and workup rules were not independently reviewed in this research pass. Published in 2022. This brief does not establish that the source is the latest guideline or that one risk framework applies to every treatment context. A recommendations document does not supply an individual patient's diagnosis, fitness assessment or treatment decision.

question_v2.title: VIALE-A — randomized-trial appraisal brief
question_v2.question: In previously untreated AML unsuitable for standard induction, what benefits, harms and applicability limits were reported for azacitidine plus venetoclax compared with azacitidine plus placebo?
question_v2.scope: AML departmental evidence review and individual applicability.
question_v2.intended_use: Inform a reviewed case-readiness pathway; no automatic treatment recommendation.

appraisal_v2.population: Original 2020 intention-to-treat analysis: 431 patients, 286 combination and 145 control; median age 76. Patients were previously untreated and considered ineligible for standard induction because of age 75 or older, coexisting conditions, or both.
appraisal_v2.intervention: Azacitidine plus venetoclax, described for evidence appraisal only; no dosing instructions are included.
appraisal_v2.outcome: Primary endpoint in the original publication: overall survival Complete remission and composite complete remission Adverse events and serious adverse events
appraisal_v2.timepoint: As reported in the dated publication; check the source version.
appraisal_v2.findings: At median follow-up 20.5 months, median overall survival was 14.7 versus 9.6 months; hazard ratio for death 0.66, 95% confidence interval 0.52–0.85. Composite complete remission was 66.4% versus 28.3%. Grade 3 or higher febrile neutropenia occurred in 42% versus 19%; serious adverse events in 83% versus 73%. Benefits and harms should be appraised together.
appraisal_v2.uncertainty: Bounded abstract/source-record appraisal. Full methods and current evidence have not been comprehensively reviewed.
appraisal_v2.limitations: The original publication's abstract and trial identifier were verified; the full paper and supplements were not appraised in this pass. The study population was unsuitable for standard induction. Results cannot be generalized automatically to all newly diagnosed AML, an individual molecular subgroup, or a patient without a documented fitness assessment. Funded by AbbVie and Genentech. The brief is a starter appraisal, not a systematic review or current treatment recommendation. The current registry lists 443 actual enrollment, a later 2021 data cutoff and last update posted2026-06-11. These are distinct from the original 2020 paper's 431-person analysis; denominators and versions must not be merged.
